message: No detected input validation: The load_dataset function only drops NA rows and compresses dtypes; there are no schema checks, dtype assertions, or value-range guards on the incoming data.
No detected untrusted source handling: Data is loaded from a local directory path (DATA_DIR_LOCAL) via pd.read_csv with no checksum verification, authentication, or integrity checks of any kind.

No detected label flipping detection: The code drops NaN rows and extracts labels but never validates label values against an expected set, checks label distributions, or uses any label-noise detection tool.

No detected data poisoning defenses: Data preparation only drops NA rows and compresses memory types; there is no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checking, or filtering of suspicious training samples.

No detected model integrity verification: The code saves a model via pickle to ARTEFACT_PATH but never loads a pretrained model, and no hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision is performed on any loaded artifact.

No detected label distribution validation: The code drops NA rows and loads data but performs no explicit class balance check, expected-label-set validation, or anomalous sample detection before training.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no trigger detection, activation-pattern analysis, or gradient anomaly detection anywhere in the training pipeline.

No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy library (Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD, etc.) is imported or applied; training uses standard scikit-learn and CatBoost without any DP mechanism.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness testing frameworks (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD, etc.) are imported or used anywhere in the evaluation code.
No detected input sanitization: The code loads data via pandas read_csv and drops NaN rows, but there are no shape/range/type validation checks on inference inputs before passing them to the model.

No detected output bounds checks: Model predictions are used directly with np.where thresholding, but there are no NaN guards, probability range checks (e.g., asserting values are within [0,1]), or other output sanity checks before returning results.

No detected prompt injection defenses: This is a tabular credit-scoring model (Logistic Regression / Random Forest / CatBoost), not an LLM, so prompt injection defenses are not applicable and not present.
